Yes. I would not do this as “LLM reads logs and summarizes.” I’d use a layered NLP pipeline so recall comes from cheap structural methods and judgment comes later. High-value strategies: - **Turn segmentation**: split by session, speaker, date, review gate, agent id, model, and tool-use blocks first. This reduces noise before any model sees text. - **Dialogue-act tagging**: classify turns as `request`, `approval`, `pushback`, `clarification`, `frustration`, `delegation`, `audit-demand`, `handoff`, `acceptance`, `course-correction`. This is much better than sentiment alone. - **Event extraction**: pull references to D1/D4, audits, review gates, roadmap changes, handoff shifts, agent launches, etc., so we can align interaction moments with initiative events. - **Role/entity extraction**: detect `Codex`, `Claude`, specific subagents, and file/phase names. That gives us “who did what” and “who caught what.” - **Lexicon sweeps**: cheap regex/keyword families for friction and positive turns. Friction: `annoy`, `unclear`, `too narrow`, `adhoc`, `sloppy`, `protocol`, `audit`, `wait`, `authorization`. Positive: `good catch`, `you’re right`, `lets do that`, `important`, `exactly`, `helpful`, `that makes sense`. - **Semantic retrieval / embeddings**: catches relevant moments that do not share keywords.
